result.recommendation: Hold approval and perform one final evidence-only gate on the exact candidate revision, then proceed directly to Step 5 if it passes.
result.rationale: The reported 9.8/10 review and 34 passing tests strongly support approval, but the checkpoint does not contain the review artifact, actual changed-path diff, type-check result, dependency diff, or line counts needed to verify the stated scope and invariants. A single bounded gate closes these audit gaps without expanding implementation scope.
must_fix: Attach or record the cycle-2 review result that substantiates the 9.8/10 score and absence of critical issues or warnings.
Verify that the actual diff is limited to the eight authorized paths.
Verify every affected module remains under 200 lines and that root production dependencies are unchanged.
Record a successful TypeScript type-check for the viewer configuration.
cautions: Passing unit and regression tests do not by themselves demonstrate File System Access behavior in supported browsers, especially permission denial, cancellation, malformed directory structures, bounded reads, and generation cancellation.
The supplied excerpts are truncated and cover only four of eight intended paths, so they cannot independently establish correctness or invariant compliance.
assumptions: The 34 reported tests ran against the same immutable revision represented by the supplied file digests.
Cycle 2 review examined the complete diff rather than only the quoted excerpts.
Browser-specific edge cases and scan-budget exhaustion are included in the viewer tests.
No relevant baseline tests were excluded from the reported commands.
success_checks: The recorded candidate revision matches the reviewed and tested revision.
The changed-file list contains only authorized paths.
Viewer type-check and all 34 reported tests pass with zero failures.
Root production dependency diff is empty.
Each affected source module is fewer than 200 lines.
The review artifact confirms a score of at least 9/10 with no blocking findings.
